key_insight: CAT-CKD combines lightweight adapter training with consensus knowledge distillation to improve skin lesion classification across datasets without accessing source data during adaptation.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help address performance drops across heterogeneous skin imaging sources, but the reported results do not establish clinical readiness.
method: Train lightweight ConvPass adapters in a frozen vision transformer using supervised contrastive learning to align source-domain features.
Combine logits from multiple source models into a consensus supervisory signal.
Adapt a student model on unlabeled target images using KL-divergence-based knowledge distillation.
evidence_signal: Across five publicly available skin lesion datasets, CAT-CKD achieved an average AUROC of 86.1%, outperforming existing MSFDA methods with 4.3 million trainable parameters.
watch_item: The abstract does not report prospective clinical validation or subgroup performance, leaving real-world reliability uncertain.
paper_title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
